content.title: The Pitt Season 3 Info: What To Know About Cast Changes, The Time Jump & More
content.text: Published Apr 16, 2026, 6:15 PM EDT Kara Hedash is the Senior Editor for Screen Rant's TV team, specializing in feature coverage for streaming releases and cable programming. Aside from overseeing a passionate team of editors and writers, Kara has years of experience in news coverage, exclusives, fan conventions, interviews, and media preview events. Before joining Screen Rant in 2019, Kara was a regular contributor for Movie Pilot, with articles also published on various other entertainment sites, such as Reel Honey, Hidden Remote, Netflix Life, AMC Theatres (via AMC Scene), and more. Reach out to Kara by emailing kara@screenrant.com Warning: Spoilers ahead for The Pitt season 2!The Pitt season 3 is officially on the way, with HBO Max confirming the renewal before season 2 premiered. Like the case with season 1, which took place over the course of one single day in September, The Pitt season 2 was set during a 15-hour shift on July 4th, making for an extra chaotic day at the Pittsburgh Trauma Medical Center's ER. For The Pitt season 2, Noah Wyle's Dr. Robby wasn't the only attending physician running the ER; Sepideh Moafi made her debut as Dr. Baran Al-Hashimi, another attending physician among The Pitt season 2's set of characters. While Robby continues to have reservations about Al-Hashimi taking over while he goes on sabbatical, it becomes clear that the character is going through something much more serious. The Pitt Season 3's Cast Changes Explained - Who Isn't Returning Seeing as The Pitt centers on a "teaching hospital," it makes sense that characters come and go during their medical career journey. However, that also means cast changes should be expected with residents, interns, and medical students, only lasting so long. Like with all TV shows, there are also surprising cast changes that stem from creative decisions. “It’s an inevitability that’s going to happen every season with this show because as writers we’re hard pressed to figure out what a lapse of time we can have and keep most of the ensemble together realistically. Emergency rooms have a high revolving door. As always, we try to bring in new characters or promote from within as we go through these cast changes and try to keep the storylines fresh, but obviously, Supriya has been a huge part of our show since the beginning.” “Dr. Mohan is a beloved character, and I love playing with her and working with Supriya, and we wish her all the best in her next endeavors, and we’re going to miss her.” Interestingly, showrunner R. Scott Gemmill revealed in an interview with TVLine that Dr. Mohan won't appear in The Pitt season 3 because "she's just not working that day." This confirms that she's still at the PTMC during season 3, making the details surrounding Supriya Ganesh's absence a bit more frustrating for fans of the character. Aside from Dr. Mohan not returning as a senior resident following The Pitt season 2's ending, the only other known cast change for The Pitt season 3 is Ayesha Harris' promotion to series regular. The announcement means that Harris' Dr. Parker Ellis,​​​​​​ who is a current night shift resident, will have a much bigger presence when the show returns next year. It will be interesting to see how season 3 will factor in other night shift characters, like fan favorite Dr. Jack Abbot, played by Shawn Hatosy. As mentioned, each season of The Pitt has focused on one particular day, with season 1 set on a day in early September, and season 2 set on July 4th the following year. All indications point to season 3 following that same format, with The Pitt showrunner R. Scott Gemmill confirming season 3's timeline will focus on November, giving the show a fourth month time jump. If The Pitt season 3 setting sticks with a November setting, the gap between seasons will be much smaller than the 10 months between seasons 1 and 2. It will also allow the upcoming season to lean into more "colder weather" storylines, which seems to be a primary factor in the November decision. The question will now be what day in November is chosen to be the shift in focus, and whether the series will want to incorporate another holiday like Thanksgiving. It's still unclear what the future holds for Dr. Robby, but Gemmill confirmed in his TVLine interview that the character does end up going on his "spirit quest" trip following The Pitt season 2 finale. The showrunner also shared that season 3 will see Robby "trying to heal." As for the other attending, Dr. Al-Hashimi is seen breaking down after her shift, and her future with the PTMC now relies on whether she can get her epilepsy under control to continue practicing medicine. Even if both take time to figure out the next chapter, the dynamics of the ER could look a lot different in season 3. Whereas season 1 heavily focused on the PittFest shooting, season 2's chaos primarily stemmed from the Fourth of July holiday and the threat of a cyberattack, forcing the hospital to go analog. With The Pitt season 3 set in November, the Pittsburgh area could realistically be dealing with snow by then, which could make for some interesting storylines. November often sees a spike in cold and flu cases, another scenario that could pack the PTMC's ER. The Pitt season 3 will surely feature some brutal storylines, including cases that mirror real-life issues facing patients, employees, and the general public. Hopefully, the new season will continue building on the intriguing relationship between characters, such as Mel's growing bond with Langdon and emerging friendship with Santos, especially after that epic karaoke credits screen to close out season 2. The Pitt Season 3 Filming & Release Date Updates Warrick Page / ©HBO MAX/ Courtesy Everett Collection In addition to revealing how The Pitt season 3 would take place in November, Gemmill also stated that filming for the new season will kick off in June. As production ramps up, more details will start to emerge, including any further cast changes and story teases. Fans will also be on the lookout for one key detail surrounding The Pitt season 3: the official release date. For reference, The Pitt season 2 began filming in June 2025 and was able to premiere the new season in January 2026. With season 3 seemingly planning to follow the same production timeline, all signs are pointing to a plausible January 2027 release for The Pitt season 3, barring any unforeseen delays. Due to The Pitt's 15-episode seasons, it would be impressive for HBO Max to successfully continue its yearly January release. Source: TVLine
